clauses.reason: All four sections of the order are decided together as the packet inventories them. Section 1 (honorary recognition or cash award by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation), section 2 (recommendation by the adopting department and award regulations), section 3 (25,000 dollar cap) and section 4 (fund transfers and procedures) have no own-terms end. EO 12107 section 2-101 amends the order by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission (effective 1979-01-01) and EO 13286 section 63 substitutes the Secretary and Department of Homeland Security for the Secretary and Department of Transportation in sections 1, 2 and 4 (effective 2003-03-01); each is an amendment that keeps the command, so the clause continues as amended. The held 10 U.S.C. 1124 text and the held eCFR 5 CFR part 451 text still refer to the order. Operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 11438 (Prescribing Procedures Governing Interdepartmental Cash Awards to the Members of the Armed Forces, December 3, 1968, 33 FR 18085), read in full from the held Federal Register text. The order has four sections that the packet inventories as one clause. Section 1 allows a suggestion, invention or scientific achievement of a member of the armed forces that is adopted by another executive department or agency to be the basis for honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transportation (Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy) or the Secretary of Defense. Section 2 lets the adopting department recommend an award and puts awards under regulations of the two Secretaries. Section 3 caps a cash award at $25,000. Section 4 requires transfer of award funds from the recommending agency and procedures set by the Civil Service Commission. The order has no date, expiry or condition. Two held later instruments amend it without ending any command: EO 12107 section 2-101 (effective January 1, 1979) substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the listed orders, and EO 11438 appears in that list; EO 13286 section 63 (effective March 1, 2003) strikes the Secretary of Transportation and the Department of Transportation and inserts the Secretary and Department of Homeland Security in sections 1, 2 and 4. The statute on which the order rests, 10 U.S.C. 1124, is still held in the U.S. Code and prints the order as a note without an ending statement, and the held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 451 names the order as of 2026-10-14. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled. Original text is a Federal Register OCR layer; the working copy of EO 13286 is the American Presidency Project transcription disclosed under the 2026-10-21 transcription ruling: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
